verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on three independent grounds, after rendering PDF pages 1138, 1139 and 1140 at 300dpi and reading the markdown directly. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind label 'missing-heading' misdescribes the finding. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:45896-45897 contains '' followed by '## D.19.4.3 Method prototypes' — the exact clause number and the exact printed title. The full body paragraph ('Method prototypes are method skeletons that define the method name, parameters, and information necessary to describe those parameters such as that specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph and the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph...'), the 'EXAMPLE:' lead-in, the calculateInterest lead sentence and the METHOD-ID./DATA DIVISION./LINKAGE SECTION. code block all transcribe verbatim against the rendered page. Zero content is lost. The sole difference is the ATX '#' count. (2) THE '#' COUNT IS A FILE-WIDE PAGE-CHUNKING ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-1140 DEFECT. Markdown heading level carries no depth information anywhere in Annex D. Measured mechanically over every Annex-D clause heading: of the 100 headings that are the FIRST clause heading to appear after a '## Page NNNN' marker, 96 are emitted at level 2 REGARDLESS of true clause depth; headings appearing later on the same page scatter across levels 2/3/4 (66/79/12). The transcription clearly converted each PDF page as an independent chunk and reset the heading baseline to '##' at each page start. That rule fully explains this trio: D.19.4.1 is mid-page on 1138 -> '###'; D.19.4.2 is the first clause heading on page 1139 -> '##'; D.19.4.3 is the ONLY clause heading on page 1140 -> '##'. The identical artifact occurs at D.2.2.2, D.2.2.5.1, D.2.3.2.3, D.2.3.2.6, D.18.2.2, D.18.3.2, D.19.3.3, D.19.5.4.2, D.19.5.4.3, D.20.3.3, D.20.4.4, D.20.5.1 and dozens more. Depth-4 clauses appear at levels 2, 3 and 4; level 2 covers depths 2 through 5. D.19.4.3 at '##' is the file's normal behavior, not an anomaly. (3) THE CLAIM'S PDF PREMISE IS TRUE BUT SELF-DEFEATING. I looked at the printed glyphs. On page 1138 the PARENT heading 'D.19.4 Methods' is set in exactly the same bold serif face and the same point size as its child 'D.19.4.1 General' directly beneath it — the two are typographically indistinguishable apart from the number. Page 1139's 'D.19.4.2 Method invocation' and page 1140's 'D.19.4.3 Method prototypes' are that same single style. Annex D of the PDF uses ONE heading style for all of depths 2-5; it does not rank D.19.4 above D.19.4.3. So the observation that D.19.4.3 is 'printed at the same typographic rank as D.19.4.1 and D.19.4.2' is correct but proves nothing, because it is equally true of the parent D.19.4. The PDF supplies no typographic evidence that D.19.4.3 belongs one level below D.19.4, and therefore no basis for calling level-2 emission a 'nesting break' against the source. In this standard the hierarchy is carried by the dotted clause number, and 'D.19.4.3' is transcribed exactly. No semantic content differs between the PDF and the markdown on this point. This is formatting furniture, and it is systemic rather than page-local, so it does not belong in a page-1140 discrepancy ledger.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading 'D.19.4.3 Method prototypes' is present in the markdown at :45897 with its clause number, title, anchor and full body text transcribed verbatim from PDF page 1140 — nothing is missing. The level-2 ATX marker is a systemic conversion artifact: the transcription resets its heading baseline to '##' at each PDF page boundary (96 of the 100 first-on-page Annex-D clause headings are level 2 irrespective of depth), so D.19.4.3 (only heading on page 1140) and D.19.4.2 (first heading on page 1139) get '##' while mid-page D.19.4.1 gets '###'. Moreover the PDF prints the parent 'D.19.4 Methods' in the identical bold face and size as 'D.19.4.1 General' — Annex D uses a single heading style for depths 2 through 5 — so the printed page asserts no rank difference between D.19.4 and D.19.4.3 for the markdown to have lost. Hierarchy is carried by the dotted clause number, which is exact. If the heading-level normalization is to be tracked at all it should be filed once as a document-wide formatting note, not as a structural finding against page 1140.
